sections.title: Pauline Corpus and the Location of Jesus's Career
sections.rationale: Covers the admissible scope of the Pauline corpus and the competing cumulative readings of whether Paul's references locate Jesus's life, death, burial, and resurrection in earthly history or permit a heavenly cosmic setting.

sections.title: The Crucifying Rulers and the Setting of Jesus's Death
sections.rationale: Covers the identity of the rulers in First Corinthians, the surrounding contrast between human and divine wisdom, the relationship to Romans 13, and whether ancient cosmology makes a crucifixion by celestial powers intelligible.

sections.title: Brothers of the Lord and Biological Kinship
sections.rationale: Covers whether Paul's references to James and other brothers of the Lord indicate biological relatives of an earthly Jesus or ordinary baptized Christians, including the limits of using later family traditions to interpret Paul.

sections.title: Luke-Acts as Historically Proximate Pauline Testimony
sections.rationale: Covers authorship, travel-companion claims, first-person narration, Pauline chronology, incidental corroboration, source use, and whether Luke-Acts can connect Paul's circle to a historically situated Jesus tradition.

sections.title: Gospel Correspondences, Independence, and Literary Dependence
sections.rationale: Covers whether interlocking Synoptic and Johannine details support independent historical grounding or are expected from literary adaptation, selective source use, and an author's narrative purposes.
